Lessons.Title: Round and Round Again
ExplanationParagraphs: Warm-up (10 minutes) is a multiplication Number Talk: calculate 5×7=35, 4×7=28, 6×7=42 and 4×8=32 mentally, explaining how a nearby number of groups or group size changes the product.

Activity 1 (15 minutes) asks for ALL whole numbers that round to 50 to nearest ten, 70 to nearest ten and 600 to nearest hundred. Apply the 2021 halfway-up rounding convention. For nearest-ten 50, the integers are 45 to 54 inclusive; 44 rounds to 40 and 55 rounds to 60.

Likewise nearest-ten 70 has inclusive integers 65 through 74. Nearest-hundred 600 has inclusive integers 550 through 649. A 10-wide rounding cell contains ten whole numbers and a 100-wide cell contains a hundred whole numbers.

Source extensions: nearest-hundred 100 includes whole numbers 50 through149; nearest-hundred 500 includes450 through549. No signed-negative or decimal interpretation is intended by this source-grade whole-number discussion.

Activity 2 (20 minutes) uses the 2021 What's My Mystery Number? partner game. Write a hidden number between100 and1,000. Supply THREE consistent clues: parity (odd/even), a number it rounds to, and a range it lies between. Other pupils guess with explanations; multiple guesses may satisfy ambiguous clues, and the teacher discusses why.

Independent Edulytics example: mystery number 746 is even, rounds to750 to nearest ten, and lies strictly between745 and747; the three clues uniquely identify746. This is NOT the original publisher mystery card.

Teacher must judge constructed lists, drawn number lines, partner talk and mystery clues; the three original image assets and Clare's gated publisher Cool-down have not been copied. Our independent exit question is goal-equivalent only.

KeyConcepts.Title: Rounding preimage
KeyConcepts.Definition: All whole numbers that yield a given rounded benchmark.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For target T and rounding step m, inclusive integers run from T-m/2 to T+m/2-1 when m is even and halfway rounds up.

KeyConcepts.Title: Halfway boundaries
KeyConcepts.Definition: A halfway integer between consecutive tens or hundreds belongs to the upper rounded interval.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mystery number clues
KeyConcepts.Definition: Parity, rounded result and an interval together constrain possible candidates.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check all three and explain whether exactly one integer survives.
KeyConcepts.Example: Even, round to750 to tens, strictly745–747 =>746.

WorkedExamples.Title: Find all values that round to 70
WorkedExamples.Question: Which whole numbers round to70 to nearest ten?
WorkedExamples.Method: Find midpoint boundaries and apply halfway-up.
Steps: 65 is halfway between60 and70, so it rounds up to70.

WorkedExamples.Title: All numbers for nearest hundred 600
WorkedExamples.Question: Find all whole numbers rounding to600 to nearest hundred.
Steps: The set contains550–649 inclusive, exactly100 integers.

WorkedExamples.Title: Create an unambiguous mystery card
WorkedExamples.Question: Propose three clues for mystery number746.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use parity, ten-rounding and close interval.
Steps: State that the number is even.
State it rounds to750 to nearest ten.
State it is strictly between745 and747.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Include55 in the set rounding to50 to nearest ten.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 55 is halfway between50 and60; the convention rounds up.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Exclude550 from values rounding to600 to nearest hundred.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 550 is halfway and assigned to the upper hundred.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Auto-grade arbitrary hidden-number clues without checking uniqueness.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: More than one number may satisfy broad clues.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Have teacher assess the clue set and explain ambiguity.

SummaryPoints: Mystery cards include odd/even, rounded benchmark and interval clues; partner reasoning is teacher-assessed.
